_why: Pin for tools/_t523-subprocess-nesting.mjs. Written from a MEASURED run, not from expectation, and specifically not from the claim in parseBpmnXml's T-337 comment ('the whole interior of an accepted element is dropped today') — which this measurement falsifies for flow nodes. Movement here is the signal: an entry changing means the editor's treatment of subProcess containment changed, which is a seam fact AEF keys records on. Element ids are deliberately absent: they are re-minted from lane and x-order on every save (T-513), so pinning them would go red on changes that mean nothing.
_finding: Re-pinned by T-1339 (T-1266 GO, slice 1) from a measured run: a subProcess and its children survive with their uids intact AND the children stay inside the subProcess; the sequenceFlow between them is written inside it too. Until T-1339 the measurement was: the children were HOISTED to <bpmn:process> level and the subProcess came back EMPTY, the flow still connecting them — nothing disappeared and the scope silently stopped existing, a structural loss no count-based instrument noticed. The canvas still draws the children flat; only the saved file keeps the nesting.
_finding_collapsed: T-528, added at AEF's request (rail 11926/11930) after they measured their own corpus: subProcess appears in three published maps and three drafts and EVERY ONE is childless, so this arm covers 100% of their real usage where the other two cover 0%. The answer is favourable and that is why it needs pinning rather than celebrating — a childless subProcess carrying only extensionElements comes back as a subProcess, not retyped to a task, and no placeholder child is injected. Their collapsed-subProcess dialect (their commit 226fe8680) is safe across this seam TODAY. What would break it is a future 'cleanup' that retypes an empty scope element, which is a defensible change someone could make without ever learning that three published maps depend on it not happening. children_after is pinned at 0 to catch the inverse defect, which would be just as silent: an editor that gives an empty scope a placeholder child changes what the map MEANS without dropping anything.
